examples.title: Measure a complete marks tree
examples.explanationHtml: Seven nodes occupy three levels: the edge height is two, and four nodes have no children.

examples.title: A chain is tall but narrow
examples.explanationHtml: Increasing insertions create a right chain. Its height is three; internal nodes have one child, so it is not full.

examples.title: Count a perfect tree level by level
examples.explanationHtml: Each complete level doubles the previous width. Through depth four, a perfect binary tree contains 31 nodes.

practice.title: Leaf count
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12) and n keys (-99..99) in complete-tree level order. Print the prompt Count and keys: then leaves=L.
hints: A leaf has no left or right child.

practice.title: Count one-child nodes
practice.statementHtml: Read a complete tree as n (0..12), then n keys (-99..99). Print Count and keys: then one-child=C.
hints: Use an exclusive-or test on the two missing links.

practice.title: Check fullness
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12) and complete-tree keys (-99..99). Print Count and keys: then full=1 if every node has zero or two children, otherwise full=0.
hints: Treat an empty tree as full.

practice.title: Perfect-tree capacity
practice.statementHtml: Read edge height h (0..20). Print Height (0..20): then leaves=L nodes=N for a perfect binary tree.
hints: Double an unsigned long width; sum the widths.

quiz.prompt: How many parents can a non-root node have in a rooted tree?
quiz.explanation: One parent gives each node a unique route from the root.

quiz.prompt: A node has children but no parent; what role does it have?
quiz.explanation: The root is identified by its missing parent, regardless of its number of children.

quiz.prompt: Which height convention makes a single-node tree height zero?
options: Count edges on the longest downward path
Count all child links in the tree
quiz.explanation: A path containing one node has zero edges.

quiz.prompt: Which shape must fill its last level from the left?
quiz.explanation: Completeness constrains level occupancy, while fullness constrains each node degree.

quiz.prompt: Can a full binary tree have exactly six nodes?
options: No, its total node count is odd
quiz.explanation: If internal nodes number I, edges are 2I and total nodes are 2I+1.

quiz.prompt: How many edges connect 9 nodes in a nonempty tree?
quiz.explanation: Every node except the root contributes its one incoming edge.

quiz.prompt: Two nodes share the same parent; what are they called?
quiz.explanation: Siblings are different children of the same parent.

quiz.prompt: A perfect tree doubles its width at each level. How many nodes are counted through edge depth 3?
quiz.explanation: The levels contain 1, 2, 4 and 8 nodes, totaling 15.

quiz.prompt: The recurrence counts edge height. What height does this two-link chain have?
quiz.explanation: The empty chain is -1, so three nodes yield two edges.

quiz.prompt: Each internal node has two children here. What leaf count follows from four internal nodes?
quiz.explanation: A full binary tree has I+1 leaves, so four internal nodes imply five leaves.

keyPoints.bn: ফুল বাইনারি ট্রিতে প্রতিটি নোডের শূন্য বা দুটো চাইল্ড থাকে।

examQuestions.question: A perfect binary tree has edge height 4. Find its leaves, total nodes and edges.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Level widths are 1,2,4,8,16. Leaves number 24=16. Total nodes number 25-1=31, and a nonempty tree has one fewer edge than nodes, giving 30 edges.

examQuestions.question: Explain full, complete and perfect with a counterexample separating full from complete.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Full means every node has zero or two children. Complete means every earlier level is filled and the last is filled from the left. Perfect means every level is filled. A root with only a left leaf is complete but not full. A root with a left leaf and a right internal node having two leaves is full but not complete.

examQuestions.question: Write a recursive function returning edge height for a linked binary tree. State time and extra space.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
int edge_height(const Node *r)
{
    if (r == NULL) { return -1; }
    int l = edge_height(r->left);
    int right = edge_height(r->right);
    return 1 + (l > right ? l : right);
}

It visits n nodes in O(n) time and keeps O(h+1) calls. A leaf returns zero.
